hero.h1: Plumbing Maintenance and Inspections in Elgin, IL
hero.sub: A sump pump that's getting loud, a water heater past its prime or a drain that's been slow for months. A maintenance visit finds the small problems before they turn into a weekend emergency. From our office on North McLean Boulevard.

img.alt: Plumber checking the drain and supply lines under a bathroom vanity during routine maintenance

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.intro: One visit, every major part of your plumbing:

steps.body: We note the heater's age from the label, test the relief valve, look for rust and drips, check the vent draft and flush out sediment if it's time.
We run the sump and any ejector pump through a full cycle and check the float, check valve, discharge line and battery backup.
We run water at every fixture, listen for gurgling and recommend a [camera look](/elgin/video-camera-sewer-inspections) only if something points to the sewer.
We look at exposed piping for corrosion and leaks and test that the main and fixture shutoffs actually close.
Silent running toilets, drips and cracked supply hoses, all quick fixes once they're found.
Everything we checked, sorted into fine, plan ahead and fix soon.

blocks.h2: Why Maintenance Pays Off in Elgin
blocks.intro: Elgin's housing ranges from the 1800s to the 2000s, and both ends benefit from regular checkups.

items.body: Homes built before 1940 often have clay sewer lines, cast iron drains and galvanized water pipe. Knowing which parts are wearing out lets you plan instead of react.
Nearly 3 in 10 homes went up between 1990 and 2009. Their first water heaters and sump pumps are past their expected life.
A spring visit tests the sump pump, backup and floor drain before heavy rain like the July 2017 storms.

blocks.h2: Plumbing Maintenance Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: When is the best time of year for a plumbing checkup in Elgin?
items.answer: Spring works best for most Elgin homes. We can test the sump pump and backup before heavy summer storms and catch any freeze damage from the winter.

items.q: My house is over 100 years old. What will you look at most closely?
items.preview: The water pipe, the drains and the sewer line.
items.answer: Galvanized supply pipe, cast iron drains and the clay sewer lateral. Those are the parts of an old system most likely to be near the end, and the summary will tell you where each one stands.

items.q: My house is from the 2000s. Is a checkup really needed?
items.preview: Yes. Original water heaters and sump pumps are past their expected life.
items.answer: Yes. The pipes are likely fine, but the water heater, sump pump and fixture parts that came with the house are often close to 20 years old or more. Replacing them on your schedule beats an emergency.
Yes. The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club) brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance visits.

items.q: Can a checkup help me plan for an old house?
items.preview: Yes. You'll know which parts are near the end.
items.answer: Yes. The summary tells you which parts of an older system are close to the end, so you can budget for them instead of reacting to a failure.

items.q: How much does a plumbing inspection cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the home and what's included. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size of the home and add-ons like a sewer camera inspection or a water heater flush. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
